chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Arthur Melrose and Jelly's recording and publishing deal
summary: Melrose, a white publisher, arranged Jelly's Victor recording and took the copyrights; Jelly cared only about getting popular and could call for cash.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: So I stayed with him until the band came all... Well, first he went into Philadelphia, and he called Arthur Melrose and told him he wanted to record. Melrose came to...
Now, who was Melrose? Say who Melrose was.
Melrose was the guy that got the recording deal for Jelly Roll Morton to record for Victor. He recorded for Brunswick, he recorded for... See, Melrose was a music publisher. And Melrose knew...

He was White. Melrose knew recording. He knew the advantage of getting recording rights on a song. And Jelly didn't know. All that Jelly wanted to do was record so he could get popular so we could go out and make some money. He didn't care, he didn't... He didn't bother about no...

...copyright. He left all that up of Melrose. But one thing about it, if he ever needed any money, all he had to do was get no the phone and call Melrose and say, "I need $500 or $1000," whatever he needed, Melrose...it would be... You could lay odds it would be there the next day.
When he knows he's going to get all his publishing rights and things.
